question: What is this entry trying to establish?
idea: The study of shapes and distances. Convex shapes have no inward dents; metric geometry asks what can be learned from distances alone. This entry studies the specific objects and conditions named in the source claim below.
why: The study of shapes and distances. Convex shapes have no inward dents; metric geometry asks what can be learned from distances alone.
exactClaim: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd admits signs keeping every partial sum within $C\sqrt d$, independently of length. Consequently every zero-sum family can be reordered with the same bound on unsigned partial sums. A matching lower bound gives the optimal order $S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)$.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
